localCandidates.questionText: A message impersonates IT support and asks you to enter your password on a fake sign-in page. Which attack is this?
localCandidates.mainTeaching: Phishing uses a deceptive message or identity to persuade someone to disclose information or take an unsafe action. It can arrive through email, text or other messaging; this question does not test a real link or message.

optionTeaching.text: Phishing uses a deceptive message or identity to persuade someone to disclose information or take an unsafe action. It can arrive through email, text or other messaging; this question does not test a real link or message.
Tailgating describes entering a restricted physical area by following another person. This scenario describes a deceptive message and fake sign-in page instead.

Shoulder surfing means observing information, such as a password, over someone’s shoulder or by similar visual observation. The attacker here is asking the recipient to disclose it through a fake page.
Dumpster diving means searching discarded material for useful information. No discarded paper, device or other waste is involved in the described message.

localCandidates.reviewRationale: Uses a concrete deceptive message rather than an email-only definition; no real phishing detection claim.

localCandidates.questionText: An attacker knows an account password but does not have its separate authentication device. Which control can require a different factor before sign-in?
localCandidates.mainTeaching: Multi-factor authentication uses different factor types, such as a password you know and an authenticator device you possess. It can stop a password-only attacker, but the MFA label alone does not guarantee protection against every phishing or session attack.

optionTeaching.text: A password hint is information that helps someone remember a password. It is not an independent authentication factor and may help an attacker guess the password.
A shared login lets multiple people use the same account. Sharing credentials does not require another factor and makes individual accountability harder.

Multi-factor authentication uses different factor types, such as a password you know and an authenticator device you possess. It can stop a password-only attacker, but the MFA label alone does not guarantee protection against every phishing or session attack.
Changing the length of a username does not require another authentication factor. Knowing the password remains the only proof in the stated password-only design.

localCandidates.reviewRationale: Makes the password-only attacker and separate possession factor explicit without promising universal phishing resistance.

localCandidates.questionText: A team wants only authorised people and systems to read its files. Which security goal does this describe?
localCandidates.mainTeaching: Confidentiality restricts access to information and its disclosure to authorised people and systems. Keeping a service online is a different goal.

optionTeaching.text: Availability is about being able to use a service or information when needed. A service can be available while still exposing files to unauthorised readers.
Confidentiality restricts access to information and its disclosure to authorised people and systems. Keeping a service online is a different goal.
Redundancy provides spare components or copies to improve resilience. Extra copies do not, by themselves, restrict who may read information.
Scalability is the ability to handle changes in workload or size. It does not define who is authorised to read a file.

localCandidates.reviewRationale: Restricts the judgment to authorised reading/disclosure, not legal privacy compliance or a deployed control.

localCandidates.questionText: A security team wants to bring logs from many systems into one place and compare events for investigation. Which listed tool is designed for this purpose?
localCandidates.mainTeaching: A Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system supports collecting and comparing security events from different sources. Useful results depend on enabled logs, relevant rules and investigation; collecting logs does not guarantee that every incident is detected.

optionTeaching.text: A Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system supports collecting and comparing security events from different sources. Useful results depend on enabled logs, relevant rules and investigation; collecting logs does not guarantee that every incident is detected.
A firewall primarily enforces traffic policy. It may produce logs, but it is not the cross-system log collection and comparison tool asked for here.
A load balancer distributes traffic or work between services. That differs from bringing security events together for investigation.
A password vault stores and manages credentials. It does not have the requested primary purpose of comparing security events from many systems.

localCandidates.reviewRationale: Generic purpose only; no current vendor capability, complete visibility or detection guarantee.

localCandidates.questionText: A control evaluates network traffic against allow and deny rules. Which listed control has this main function?
localCandidates.mainTeaching: A firewall evaluates network traffic using its configured rules and allows or blocks traffic accordingly. Firewall types differ, and permitted traffic can still contain harmful activity.

optionTeaching.text: A firewall evaluates network traffic using its configured rules and allows or blocks traffic accordingly. Firewall types differ, and permitted traffic can still contain harmful activity.
A cryptographic hash produces a digest for a data input. It does not itself enforce network allow and deny rules.
A digital certificate binds a public key to identity information under an issuer’s signature. It is not the device or service enforcing these traffic rules.
A backup is a retained copy used to support recovery. Keeping a backup does not filter live network traffic.

localCandidates.reviewRationale: Does not assume every firewall tracks connections or guarantees attack prevention.

localCandidates.questionText: A service owner says losing more than 15 minutes of recent records after an outage is unacceptable. Which recovery target describes that limit?
localCandidates.mainTeaching: Recovery Point Objective (RPO) expresses the tolerable amount of recent data loss as a time window. Here the target is 15 minutes of records; whether a usable recovery point meets it must be checked, not assumed from a backup schedule.

optionTeaching.text: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is the target time for restoring the service. It answers how long recovery may take, rather than how much recent data may be lost.

Recovery Point Objective (RPO) expresses the tolerable amount of recent data loss as a time window. Here the target is 15 minutes of records; whether a usable recovery point meets it must be checked, not assumed from a backup schedule.
Mean Time to Repair or Recover (MTTR) is an average repair or recovery duration, with the exact expansion defined by the organisation. It is not the tolerable recent-data-loss window.
Single Loss Expectancy (SLE) estimates the loss from one event, usually in money. It is not a recovery-point target measured in minutes of records.

localCandidates.reviewRationale: Separates a time-based data-loss target from restoration time, an average duration and a monetary estimate.

localCandidates.questionText: A reporting account receives only the read access needed for its assigned task. Which principle does this illustrate?
localCandidates.mainTeaching: Least privilege limits an account to the permissions needed for its assigned work. Naming the principle does not prove that a real permission set has been reviewed or correctly enforced.

optionTeaching.text: Least privilege limits an account to the permissions needed for its assigned work. Naming the principle does not prove that a real permission set has been reviewed or correctly enforced.
Open access broadly permits access instead of limiting it to the account’s assigned task. That is the opposite of the restriction described here.
Job rotation changes who performs duties over time. It does not, by itself, limit the permissions held by this reporting account.
High availability keeps a service usable despite failures. It does not decide which reports an account is allowed to read.

localCandidates.reviewRationale: Same introductory recognition family as the guest MCQ; do not count the two as independent evidence.

localCandidates.questionText: A trusted publisher provides a SHA-256 digest for the exact file version you download. You hash the downloaded file bytes with SHA-256 and get a different digest. Which check has failed?
localCandidates.mainTeaching: The integrity comparison failed: the downloaded bytes do not match the trusted expected digest for that file version using the same algorithm. A mismatch does not explain whether the cause is corruption, a different file or malicious change, and a digest supplied by an attacker would not establish publisher authenticity.

optionTeaching.text: Availability concerns being able to obtain or use the file or service. The file was downloaded and hashed; this result concerns whether its bytes match the expected version.

The integrity comparison failed: the downloaded bytes do not match the trusted expected digest for that file version using the same algorithm. A mismatch does not explain whether the cause is corruption, a different file or malicious change, and a digest supplied by an attacker would not establish publisher authenticity.
Confidentiality concerns preventing unauthorised disclosure. A hash mismatch does not show that anyone read the file.

Authentication concerns verifying an identity or source. The stated comparison assumes a trusted reference and checks file integrity; the mismatch alone does not identify a person or prove an authentication failure.

localCandidates.reviewRationale: Adds trusted expected version, identical algorithm and file-byte input. Does not infer an attacker or authenticity from a bare digest.

localCandidates.questionText: Responders confirm ransomware is spreading between office computers. Their approved plan authorises network isolation, and no safety-critical service depends on those connections. Which action best limits further network spread now?
localCandidates.mainTeaching: Isolate the affected systems as authorised by the response plan to reduce further network spread. Coordinate the response and continue checking other systems: isolation does not remove the malware or prove that the whole incident is contained.

optionTeaching.text: Isolate the affected systems as authorised by the response plan to reduce further network spread. Coordinate the response and continue checking other systems: isolation does not remove the malware or prove that the whole incident is contained.
Deleting every log removes information needed to understand and investigate the incident. It does not stop the network connections carrying the spread.
Immediate payment does not isolate affected computers or guarantee a working decryptor, data recovery or an end to the incident. It does not meet the stated containment task.
Restarting every server indiscriminately can disrupt services and lose volatile evidence without closing the paths used for spread. Follow the supplied authorised isolation plan instead.

localCandidates.reviewRationale: Adds confirmation, authority, network-spread goal and safety premise; rejects a universal first action or guaranteed containment.

localCandidates.questionText: A reporting user can read only the reports needed for their assigned work. Which principle does this illustrate?
localCandidates.mainTeaching: Least privilege gives a user or account only the access needed for its assigned work. This terminology check does not prove that a real system enforces the correct permissions.

optionTeaching.text: Least privilege gives a user or account only the access needed for its assigned work. This terminology check does not prove that a real system enforces the correct permissions.
Tailgating refers to following someone into a restricted physical area. It does not describe limiting this user’s access to reports.
Piggybacking is also used for following another person through an access point, with terminology that can overlap tailgating. It is not the minimum-permissions principle asked for here.

localCandidates.reviewRationale: Shares the introductory least-privilege family with the reporting-account starter. No universal consent distinction between the two physical-entry terms is required.

localCandidates.questionText: Practice-only scenario: ransomware is confirmed on ordinary office computers and is still spreading over the network. The approved plan authorises isolating affected computers; assume no safety-critical service depends on those connections. Before restoring services, responders must address the identified malware and its entry path. Verified clean backups are available, and restored services must be checked before reconnection. Arrange these three work packages for this stated plan.
localCandidates.mainTeaching: For this supplied plan, containment limits further spread, eradication addresses the known cause, and recovery restores and verifies services. Real response activities can overlap; this is a bounded plan-recognition exercise, not a universal linear incident model or evidence of successful containment.

stepTeaching.label: Contain
stepTeaching.text: Use the authorised isolation to reduce further network spread; continue coordination and assessment.

stepTeaching.label: Eradicate
stepTeaching.text: Address identified malware and its entry path, then check that the known cause has been removed.

stepTeaching.label: Recover
stepTeaching.text: Restore from verified clean backups and check service operation before reconnecting under the plan.

permutationTeaching.text: Correct for this supplied plan: limit further spread, address the known cause, then restore and verify services. Communication, investigation and evidence work may continue throughout.

Containment is already first in your sequence. The remaining error is restoring before addressing the identified malware and entry path, which can expose the restored service again. Put eradication before recovery for this plan.
This sequence starts cleanup while the affected computers can still spread ransomware. The supplied plan authorises safe network isolation first; then address the identified cause before recovery.
Both cleanup and restoration occur before the authorised isolation in this sequence. First reduce the continuing network spread, then address the known cause and restore verified services.
Recovery begins before limiting spread or addressing the identified cause. A restored service can be exposed again. Use the authorised containment, then eradication, before recovery under this plan.

Recovery is first and containment last, leaving both dependencies unmet at restoration time. Reduce continuing spread, address the known cause, and only then restore and verify services under this plan.

localCandidates.reviewRationale: Adds explicit fictional network-spread, authority, safety and restoration dependencies. Feedback distinguishes the already-contained wrong order. Shares response content with the starter and bank rather than creating independent evidence.
